evidence.title: App Events: See app usage and performance data in your Dev Dashboard

Interpretation: these sources support two distinct 'open' concepts—an App Store listing 'Open app button' event and in-app/app-usage events developers instrument themselves.

evidence.title: Research conclusion
evidence.excerpt: External research from official Shopify sources supports these observed capabilities: (1) the Dev Dashboard shows logs, health metrics, and app events that the app sends to Shopify; (2) App Events are developer-sent instrumentation for merchant behavior, feature adoption, and app-specific actions; (3) listing-traffic measurement is optional and documented via GA4/Facebook Pixel plus App Listing events such as 'Open app button'; (4) the provided official sources do not confirm a built-in, universal app-open metric that exists without developer instrumentation. Interpretation: if the goal is to evaluate post-change app opens broadly, the best-supported source is developer-defined App Events in Dev Dashboard, while listing-page 'Open app button' only measures that specific listing CTA interaction, not all app opens.

limitations: The conclusion is bounded to the supplied official Shopify citations and one allowed tool call; no additional lookup was available to search for undocumented or newly published metrics pages.

The evidence confirms App Listing page 'Open app button' tracking and developer-sent App Events, but absence of evidence in these sources is not absolute proof that no other Shopify metric exists elsewhere.
The sources support measurement options conceptually, but do not quantify retention windows, reporting granularity, or exact dashboard field names for a universal 'app open' KPI.

m4.competingExplanation: A competing explanation is trust friction after impression: the listing has 0 reviews and does not make read-only safety prominent near the access decision, which could suppress opens even if discovery is adequate.
